## Rule

Input contains a small hollow square in color `V` plus four color-5 guide markers outside it. Draw the larger rectangle one cell inside the guide markers, using the dominant non-background/non-5 color `V`, while preserving the original input elsewhere.

## Algorithm sketch

1. Use separable `Einsum` scans over the full input with shared `[10]` channel-5 and `[30]` first-15-position selectors to detect gray-marker presence by row/column.
2. Cast the scan sums through BOOL to `UINT8` before `ArgMax(select_last_index=0/1)` so duplicate side-marker rows/columns do not beat the true outer guides.
3. Encode 15-cell row/column categories as rank-2 `UINT8` vectors (`outside`, `inside`, `edge`) and Pad them to `[30,1]` / `[1,30]`.
4. Use one broadcast `Greater` to make the full 30x30 rectangle border, use masked channel presence as the paint one-hot, and emit `Where(border, paint_color, input)` as graph output.

## Cost analysis

Canonical cost is dominated by six `[1,10,16,16]` F32 tensors (`input_inner`, `outer_frame`, `ch0p`, `mult`, `mi`, `output_inner`) at 10,240 bytes each. The 9-Conv bank itself is not the main byte sink; most Conv/row/col outputs are only 64 bytes.

Winning lever in v1: avoid materializing the 10-channel output assembly. Compute only a single-channel bool border mask and make the final broadcast `Where(border, paint_color, input)` the graph output so the full `[1,10,30,30]` result is excluded from memory.

Further wins: replace the 16x16 color-5 slice with two separable `Einsum` scans (`nchw,c,w->nh` and `nchw,c,h->nw`) using a shared channel-5 selector and shared first-15-position selector. This keeps the 120-byte scan outputs but cuts scan params from 300 dense Conv elements to 40 selector elements. Use `ArgMax` for first/last guide indices instead of weighted reductions. Build the border with one broadcast `Greater` over `UINT8` row/column category codes, avoiding extra full-canvas bool masks. Use non-bg/non-5 channel presence rather than full color counts because the generator has one paint color.

## Don't-do log

- Do not spend the first pass on blanket F16 conversion; prior PR_HUGE attempt found Cast/load overheads and no winner.
- Do not trust the crop advisory literally. The parent already starts with a 16x16 Slice; the real 30x30 tensor is the final output, which the scorer excludes.
- Do not assume fusing the row/column Conv bank is the primary lever. Per-tensor scoring shows the bank is small; the output assembly was the expensive part.
- Do not use bool-valued `Where` for mask fusion; ONNX checker accepts it, but local ORT has no implementation for that `Where(9)` case.
- Do not use sparse initializers for the scan weights; ORT may run them, but `check_model(full_check=True)`/shape inference fails, so the official scorer rejects the model.
- Do not drop the scan-sum saturation before `ArgMax`. Direct F32 `ArgMax` scores 1,928 but fails byte-equivalence because duplicate side markers can make an interior row/column sum to 2 and beat the true outer guide rows/columns.
